Answer: B
Reason: The chest radiograph demonstrates volume loss in the right hemithorax with a mediastinal shift towards the right and an abnormal vascular course (kinked vessel) in the right cardiophrenic angle, which are characteristic findings of right upper lobe pulmonary hypoplasia. Options suggesting leftward shift or hyperinflation contradict the visible ipsilateral volume loss.
